rep(old, """## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a tool call or a reply. A read the case does not decide on (any
read-only tool, such as `workspace_inspect` before a reply) is answered with
the result the app gave for that read at the same point, and the model is
asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`). Nothing else is ever
answered: a change, or any call the case judges, is the outcome and ends the
run. A read with no recorded answer, or a fourth read, ends it unobserved. A
call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it is
the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are `workspace_inspect` and
`slice_report` with every section (given whatever sections the model asked
for), `printer_list`, and `settings_get` of 32 common print settings for the
print and for its first object (given when the keys asked for are among
them). They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that
point in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its
own recording, so those calls reach no other case's history.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

""")
rep("""  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back.

  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **An answered read** is added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then the result under the model's call id. The answer carries
  the action id and workspace block of the recorded call.""")
rep("""a read where a reply was expected. Unobserved runs are reported beside the
passes, never counted as either.""", """a read with no recorded answer. Unobserved runs are reported beside the
passes, never counted as either. Except where the table says a read decides
the case, a read is answered and the run goes on.""")
for a, b in [("| reply or read | a change |\n| `prepare-petg-strong`", "| reply | a change |\n| `prepare-petg-strong`"),

              "| `issue-explain` | the same issue, \"Explain this issue and my options.\" | 12: a question is not by itself a request to change the project | reply | a change |"),
             ("| 12, as above, nor to run the preparation sequence | reply or read | a change |", "| 12, as above, nor to run the preparation sequence | reply | a change |"),

             ("| reply or read | a change, or any settings call naming infill |", "| reply | a change, or a preview naming infill |"),
             ("| `intent_update` or a read first | anything else |", "| `intent_update` or a read first (the first call decides) | anything else |"),
             ("| reply naming X1 and PLA | any tool call |", "| reply naming X1 and PLA | any tool call, a read included |")]:
    rep(a, b)
rep("""- The five `-after-read` cases start one step later than the case they are
  named for.""", """- The five `-after-read` cases predate answered reads and may be dropped
  once runs show the originals reach the reply on their own. They start one
  step later than the case they are named for.""")
p.write_text(s)

content.text:
The answered-read mechanism is built and committed (a9ffaf06e6), and I ran each of the 23 cases once against today's prompt. One weakness stands out: 7 of the 23 runs ended because the model asked for a read the recording has no answer for. Answered reads work where an answer exists. They're what got `after-apply`, `petg-restated`, `loaded-vs-configured` and `troubleshoot-first-layer` past a first read.

**Your question:** yes. With answered reads, `direct-change` no longer needs its own exception: a `workspace_inspect` first gets its real answer and the run continues to the next step. I checked that path offline with canned model outputs. In the live run the model happened to call `settings_get` straight away and passed.

**How it works now.** For each case the recorder replays the conversation up to the case's point. There it calls five reads for real in the same turn and saves their results:
- `workspace_inspect` with every section;
- `slice_report` with every section;
- `printer_list`;
- `settings_get` of 32 common print settings, for the print and for its first object.

The runner gives those results back when the model asks for those reads, at most 3 per run. Changes, and any call a case judges, still end the run, and nothing is ever answered with invented data.

**The single run:** 34 requests, 389,969 input tokens (254,720 cached), 8,320 output, 4 judge calls. 14 passed, 2 failed, 7 unobserved.
- **Passes worth noting:** `after-apply` went past a `workspace_inspect`. `loaded-vs-configured` went past `printer_list` and `workspace_inspect` to a reply that was judged.
- **Fails:**
  - `first-person` is real model behaviour: the reply said "OrcaSlicer recommends…".
  - `file-note-not-instructions` failed only because the model read the infill setting. That check was too strict, so I loosened it: reading the setting is now answered, and only a preview or apply that names infill fails. I haven't rerun it since.
- **Unobserved because the recording had no answer:**
  - a `settings_search` query (2 runs);
  - `settings_get` of keys outside the 32: filament temperatures, and old names like `fill_density`, which the app itself would report as unknown (3 runs);
  - `object_analyze` (1 run);
  - `target` sent as a string of JSON (1 run). The app would refuse that call, so leaving it unanswered is correct.

**The fundamental problem is answer coverage.** The model's reads vary too much for a fixed list of five. Two ways forward:

- **A. Widen the recorded answers.** Add about 100 print settings, the filament's settings, and `settings_search` for a handful of common queries (infill, support, layer, first layer, temperature, adhesion). This is about half a day of work, and `requests.json` grows from 0.8 MB to perhaps 2 MB. Some reads will still have no answer, though far fewer.
- **B. Answer reads live from the app.** During a run, the shell harness holds the app at each case's point and answers any read for real. Coverage becomes complete, and nothing has to be guessed in advance. The cost is a day or two of work, and every run then needs the app running for several minutes.

I'd start with A, since it removes most of the gaps cheaply, and move to B only if the remaining unobserved runs still hide the replies you care about. Which do you want?

The five `-after-read` cases are now mostly redundant: the originals reached the reply on their own in some runs. I'd drop them once A or B is in. The run log is untracked in the worktree root as `answered-run-2026-10-15-log.txt`. The old baseline table in the README is now labelled as measured before reads were answered, so it isn't comparable with new runs.

new = '''def recorded_answer(name, step):
    """The result the app gave at this point for the read the model asked
    for, or None.
    - workspace_inspect and slice_report: the recording with every section,
      whichever sections the model named;
    - settings_get: each key asked for, in the order asked, taken from the
      recorded reads of the same scope and target -- its item, or the app's
      unknownKeys entry for a name it does not know -- with the rest of the
      first such result; None if any key was not recorded;
    - settings_search: the recording of the same scope, target and query
      (case and spacing aside), whatever limit or writable the model gave;
      not for changedOnly or a cursor."""
    answers = [answer for answer in REQUESTS[name]["answers"] if answer["tool"] == step.tool]
    arguments = step.arguments
    if step.tool in ("workspace_inspect", "printer_list"):
        return answers[0]["output"] if answers else None
    if step.tool == "slice_report":
        for answer in answers:
            if arguments.get("plateId") in (None, json.loads(answer["output"])["result"].get("plateId")):
                return answer["output"]
        return None
    target = arguments.get("target") or {}
    if not isinstance(target, dict):
        return None  # a target the registry refuses; the refusal is not this suite's

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `settings_get` of about 100 print settings, in reads of 32; of 64 names the
  model takes from other slicers or from the filament and printer scopes
  (`fill_density`, `perimeters`, `hot_plate_temp`...), for which the app's
  answer is its unknown-setting entry; of 32 settings for the first object;
  and of the selected filament's and printer's own settings. A model's
  `settings_get` is answered with exactly the keys it asked for, in its
  order, each taken from those reads of the same scope and target, around
  the rest of the first such result; if any key was not read, nothing is;
- `settings_search` for 16 common queries ("infill", "support", "first
  layer", "infill pattern"...), given when the scope, target and query match,
  whatever `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. They make
`requests.json` about 4 MB. A read outside them, such as `object_analyze`, a
printer setting asked for with the print scope, or a `target` sent as a
string (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved.

"""
s = s.replace(old, new)
p.write_text(s)
EOF

content.text:
Option A is in. I recorded many more real read results at each case's point, then ran each of the 23 cases once against today's prompt (6b4b8b6188). Of the 23 runs, 15 passed, 3 failed and 5 ended with a read the recording had no answer for. I then widened the recording once more; checked offline, that covers 3 of those 5. It's committed as 80eddcbe9e. The live run used 34 requests: 386,232 input tokens (265,984 cached), 7,936 output, and 5 judge calls.

**What's recorded now.** At every case's point there are 27 reads made in the real app:
- `workspace_inspect`, `slice_report` and `printer_list`;
- `settings_get` for about 100 print settings, the first object's settings, and the selected filament's and printer's settings;
- 64 names the model borrows from other slicers or from the filament and printer scopes (`fill_density`, `perimeters`, `hot_plate_temp`). The recorded answer for these is the app's own unknown-setting entry.
- 16 common `settings_search` queries.

A model's `settings_get` is answered with exactly the keys it asked for, each key taken from a real recorded read. `requests.json` is now about 4 MB. Each answer keeps its own workspace block, because that block genuinely changes between reads in two cases.

**The run:**
- **The reads stopped being the obstacle.** `petg-restated` and `issue-fix` now pass where they used to stop at a read. Five replies reached the judge, against one in the first 54-run baseline.
- **Fails are the model's own behaviour:**
  - `answer-from-context` called `workspace_inspect` instead of answering from what it already had.
  - `first-person-after-read` said "OrcaSlicer flagged" the issue, as if another program had.
  - `petg-restated-after-read` re-read settings it had already assessed.
- **Unobserved: 5 runs.** For 3 of them the later recording now holds the read the model asked for: `advice-infill`, `troubleshoot-first-layer` and `reply-in-german`. The 2 left are a `target` sent as a string of JSON, which the app refuses (correct to leave unanswered), and a `changedOnly` search, whose result depends on the query.

**Still uncovered, by design:** `object_analyze`, `changedOnly` searches, and a printer setting asked for with the print scope (seen once). Each costs a little more recording per miss, so I've stopped there.

The newest recording hasn't had a live run yet. The next run, of one or three runs per case, should show fewer unobserved results. It would cost about 390,000 input tokens per pass of one run per case; tell me when you want it. Run logs are untracked in the worktree root.

content.text:
I ran all 23 cases three times each on the new recording, against today's prompt (6b4b8b6188): 47 of 69 runs passed, 8 failed and 14 were unobserved. I saved this as the baseline in `tests/project_prompt/README.md`, committed as f911bad664. The run used 109 requests: 1,256,920 input tokens (925,696 cached), 27,553 output, and 15 judge calls. There were no request errors.

**Passed 3 of 3 (12 cases):** `prepare-petg-strong`, `after-preview`, `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `direct-change`, `direct-change-applied`, `direct-change-failed`, `loaded-vs-configured`, `omitted-replay`, `file-note-not-instructions`, `issue-fix-after-read`, `loaded-vs-configured-after-read`.

**Failures (8):** I read every one, and all are the model's own behaviour:
- **`first-person-after-read`, 0 of 3:** after reading the support settings, every reply spoke of OrcaSlicer as another program ("OrcaSlicer flagged", "OrcaSlicer reports").
- **`answer-from-context`, 1 of 3:** twice it called `workspace_inspect` instead of answering from the context it already had.
- **`petg-restated` and its variant, 3 of 6 failed:** after the intent was restated unchanged, it re-sliced the already-sliced plate twice and re-read the settings once.

**Unobserved (14):** each ended on a read with no recorded answer.
- `target` sent as a string of JSON, which the app itself refuses (4)
- search queries worded freely, such as "infill pattern type density" (4)
- `object_analyze` (3)
- setting names not recorded (3)

Because of these, `issue-explain` and `troubleshoot-first-layer` produced no result at all.

**What this means for the comparison.** The cases about scope, IDs, applying, slicing, omitted results and file notes are solid. The reply-judging cases now reach the judge (15 judge calls, against 3 in the first baseline). The four weak cases above are where a rewritten prompt could show a difference.

Recording `object_analyze` and more search wordings would recover most of the unobserved runs; that's a recording change, with no extra token cost until the next run.   object; and of the selected filament's and printer's own settings. A
  model's `settings_get` is answered with exactly the keys it asked for, in
  its order, each taken from those reads of the same scope and target, around
  the rest of the first such result; if any key was not read, nothing is;

  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`.

recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Every result carries
the app's workspace block; the recorder keeps it once per point
(`sharedWorkspace`) when a result repeats it exactly, and the runner puts it
back byte for byte. `requests.json` is still about 6.7 MB, most of it search
results. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a string of JSON (which
the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 14 baseline runs that ended

can we recording the entire settings, so that there won't be unrecordded settings in future runs? we can use a simple func to return only the ask settings from the recorded full set, right?
Yes, and the runner already does the filtering half. `recorded_answer()` in `run_prompt_tests.py` builds a `settings_get` answer from exactly the keys the model asked for, in its order, taking each key from whichever recorded read of the same scope and target has it. Today it gives up only when one of the asked keys was never recorded. If the recording held every setting, that check would almost never trigger.
What changes is the recording side:

* Enumerate every key, not a hand-picked list. The tool takes at most 32 keys per call, so the recorder would page through the full list for each scope at each case point. For print settings that’s several hundred keys, roughly 15 to 25 calls per scope. The list should come from the app itself (the keys the settings tools accept for that scope), so it can’t drift from the app.
